root_cause.text: `drivers/mux/mmio.c` manually created an MMIO regmap with `regmap_init_mmio()` during `mux_mmio_probe()` but never freed it on probe failure or driver detach, causing a resource leak in the mux/mmio subsystem.
root_cause.evidence: The patch comment says “The mmio regmap that may be allocated during probe is never freed,” and the diff changes `regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)` to `devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)`, explicitly making the regmap device-managed so it is released on probe failures and unbind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch MMIO regmap initialization to the devm-managed API so the regmap is automatically cleaned up on device removal.
intent_record.what: In mux_mmio_probe(), the call to initialize the MMIO regmap was changed from regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg) to devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg).
intent_record.how: The regmap is now managed by the device-managed resource framework, so it will be automatically released when the device is detached, reducing the risk of resource leaks while preserving the same probe-time initialization behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Switch MMIO regmap initialization to the devm-managed API so the regmap is automatically cleaned up on device removal.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the reported resource leak by replacing manual regmap initialization with the devm-managed API, which ensures the MMIO regmap is automatically freed on probe failure or driver detach.

candidates.rationale: This manually creates an MMIO regmap without devm ownership, so if probe later fails or the driver is detached, the regmap is not automatically released, directly causing the resource leak described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line manually allocates an MMIO regmap without devm-managed lifetime handling. As described in the root cause, the regmap could be leaked on probe failure or driver removal because it was never automatically freed.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 61de83fd8256e185588670d3cf0bccc3e913819c
Author: Andrew Davis <afd@ti.com>
Date:   Thu Jan 23 12:20:59 2025 -0600

    mux: mmio: Do not use syscon helper to build regmap
    
    The syscon helper device_node_to_regmap() is used to fetch a regmap
    registered to a device node. It also currently creates this regmap
    if the node did not already have a regmap associated with it. This
    should only be used on "syscon" nodes. This driver is not such a
    device and instead uses device
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the old use of `device_node_to_regmap(np)` to implicitly create a regmap, which is no longer present here. The probe now explicitly maps the resource with `devm_platform_ioremap_resource(pdev, 0)` and then creates the regmap with `regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)`, as shown by `else { base = devm_platform_ioremap_resource(pdev, 0); ... regmap = regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg); }`. This means the specific bug-inducing helper misuse is absent and the code already contains the corrected handling. Although the snippet does not show cleanup paths, the question is about whether this function contains the vulnerable construct and whether the fix is present; the shown code clearly has the fix.
